scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation shows more disputed bills have actual reads (1785) than estimated reads (1240), indicating that disputes are not driven primarily by estimation substitution.

problem_definition.root_problem: Recent changes to billing import validation rules have introduced systematic billing errors that produce incorrect bills for actual meter reads, leading to increased dispute tickets.

trace.summary: Recent changes to billing import validation rules have introduced systematic billing errors that produce incorrect bills for actual meter reads, leading to increased dispute tickets.

An agent is still needed to monitor billing import validation rule changes in real time and to flag any unauthorized modifications, because manual audits may not catch regressions quickly enough to prevent further wrong bills.

structural_remedies.description: Revert billing import validation rules to the version prior to the recent changes identified in DA-RULES and lock the rule set pending formal change‑control approval. [A-A1][A-A2][A-A3][E-03]
structural_remedies.rationale: Rollback is a configuration change, not a bill write, so it complies with K-BILLWRITE; 225 minutes remain in the contest budget.; residual gap: Verification that the rule set has actually been changed (U-U1) remains open; requires audit of DA-RULES to confirm current version.

structural_remedies.description: Introduce a mandatory change‑control gate for any modification to billing import validation rules, requiring Billing Operations (SH‑BILL) approval and documentation in DA-RULES before deployment. [K-BILLWRITE]
structural_remedies.rationale: Adds an approval step; does not require automated bill writes, thus respects K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH.; residual gap: Does not correct bills already issued; residual gap is the need to rebill or credit affected accounts, which is prohibited by K-BILLWRITE without manual approval.

solution_design.why_agent: An agent is still needed to monitor billing import validation rule changes in real time and to flag any unauthorized modifications, because manual audits may not catch regressions quickly enough to prevent further wrong bills.
solution_design.bridge_sunset_condition: If structural remedies SR-R1 or SR-R2 are not deployed within the remaining contest budget (225 minutes), the agent must continue monitoring DA-RULES for changes and alert on any unauthorized modification.
